issues.title: Documentation references npm instead of yarn
issues.description: The rule requires all package management commands to use yarn, but the code documentation references npm commands for installing and running Tinybird tools
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
/**
 * Service for managing Tinybird JWT tokens and authentication
 *
 * To run Tinybird tests locally:
 * npm install -g @tinybird/cli
 * npm run docker:dev:analytics

issues.rule_name: Package Manager Must Be Yarn v1

issues.title: Token caching stores entire object instead of token string
issues.description: In the getToken method, when caching the JWT token, the code now stores the entire tokenData object (containing both 'token' and 'exp' properties) instead of just extracting the token string. This causes the returned token structure to be malformed as {token: {token: string, exp: number}, exp: number} instead of the expected {token: string, exp: number}. This will break any consumers of the Tinybird API (like the /api/tinybird/token endpoint and stats/tinybird.js) that expect a string token value, causing authentication failures when making requests to Tinybird pipes.

issues.title: JWT signature validation bypassed in token expiration check
issues.description: The _isJWTExpired method now uses jwt.decode() instead of jwt.verify() to check token expiration. While jwt.verify() validates the token's signature and ensures it hasn't been tampered with, jwt.decode() only decodes the token without any cryptographic validation. This creates a security vulnerability where expired, tampered, or forged tokens could be accepted as valid. An attacker could potentially modify token claims (like extending expiration or changing site_uuid in scopes) and the system would accept the malicious token, bypassing authentication controls for Tinybird API access.

issues.title: JWT token structure changed by removing noTimestamp option
issues.description: The _generateToken method previously created JWT tokens with {noTimestamp: true} to exclude the 'iat' (issued at) claim from the token payload. This option has been removed, causing the JWT library to automatically include the 'iat' timestamp in the token. This changes the token structure that Tinybird expects and may cause authentication failures if Tinybird's API validates or expects a specific token payload structure without the 'iat' claim. The changed token format could also affect token caching behavior and invalidate existing token validation logic.

issues.title: Type mismatch in _isJWTExpired call after token caching change
issues.description: The _isJWTExpired method expects a string token parameter, but after line 98 changes this._serverToken from storing just the token string to storing the entire tokenData object, line 96 now passes an object {token: string, exp: number} to _isJWTExpired instead of a string. This causes jwt.decode() at line 164 to fail when trying to decode an object instead of a JWT string. The method will always return true (treating the token as expired) on subsequent calls, forcing unnecessary token regeneration on every request and breaking the token caching mechanism entirely.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25477 - Removed unused tinybird filters

structured_output.summary:
The description says this PR only removes the unused `device`, `browser` and `os` filters from the Tinybird pipes (`api_kpis`, `api_top_locations`, `api_top_pages`, `filtered_sessions`). It also deletes the matching YAML tests and repoints the "multiple filters combined" tests to `source` + `pathname`. Separately, it drops `api_top_browsers`, `api_top_devices` and `api_top_os` from the JWT scope list. The Tinybird part is clean, and the endpoint pipes for those three resources are already gone from `endpoints/`.

The PR also makes three changes to JWT handling in `TinybirdService.js` that the description doesn't mention, and one of them breaks things. `getToken()` now stores the whole `{token, exp}` object in `this._serverToken` instead of the token string. When JWT auth is on, every caller now gets an object back in `token`. The server-side stats requests send `Bearer [object Object]`, and the admin `/tinybird/token` endpoint returns an object where clients expect a JWT string. On top of that, the expiry check can't read the object, so caching stops working and a new token is signed on every call. The other two changes (dropping `noTimestamp`, and switching `jwt.verify` to `jwt.decode`) don't seem needed for a filter cleanup. The existing unit tests miss all of this because they only check that `token` is truthy.
structured_output.verdictRationale: `getToken()` now returns an object instead of a JWT string, which breaks every Tinybird request made with JWT auth. That alone blocks merge. The other JWT changes aren't in the PR's scope and should be reverted or explained.

architecture.overview:
Ghost's analytics run on Tinybird. Ghost-side services call Tinybird endpoint pipes (`api_kpis`, `api_top_*`) over HTTP, and many of those pipes reuse the `filtered_sessions` pipe for session-level filtering. Authentication goes through `TinybirdService`. When a workspace ID and admin token are configured, it signs a JWT whose scopes list each allowed pipe and fix `site_uuid` to the site. It caches that JWT in memory and hands it out to `stats/utils/tinybird.js` (server-side queries) and to the admin API endpoint `api/endpoints/tinybird.js`, which passes it on to the stats front end.

The PR removes the `device`, `browser` and `os` WHERE clauses from the pipes, along with their YAML tests. It also removes the three dropped `api_top_*` pipes from the JWT scope list. Beyond that, it changes the token lifecycle in `TinybirdService`: the cache now holds the whole `{token, exp}` object, tokens are signed with an `iat` claim, and the expiry check decodes the token without verifying the signature.
steps: Start at `TinybirdService.getToken()`. It's the only way callers get Tinybird credentials, either a JWT or the static local/stats tokens.
`_generateToken()` builds the JWT payload, with one `PIPES:READ` scope per entry in `TINYBIRD_PIPES`. The PR removes `api_top_browsers`, `api_top_devices` and `api_top_os` from that list.
Before reusing the cached `_serverToken`, `getToken()` checks it with `_isJWTExpired()`. The PR changes both what gets cached and how it's checked.
The token is used in two places: `stats/utils/tinybird.js#buildRequest` sends it as a bearer token, and `api/endpoints/tinybird.js` returns it to the admin client.
On the Tinybird side, the endpoint pipes and `pipes/filtered_sessions.pipe` drop their `device`/`browser`/`os` clauses. The `tests/*.yaml` fixtures are updated to match.

findings.title: getToken() caches the {token, exp} object instead of the JWT string
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/server/services/tinybird/TinybirdService.js` line 98, `getToken()` sets `this._serverToken = tokenData`, but `tokenData` is the `{token, exp}` object. As a result, `getToken().token` is an object instead of a JWT string, and the expiry check never hits the cache. Change it back to `this._serverToken = tokenData.token`. Then tighten `ghost/core/test/unit/server/services/tinybird/TinybirdService.test.js` (the `getToken` describe block, around lines 118-150). Assert that `typeof result.token === 'string'` and that `jwt.verify(result.token, adminToken)` succeeds. Also assert that two calls inside the buffer window return the identical token string, which proves caching works.

findings.title: Unrelated JWT changes: noTimestamp removed and verify replaced by decode
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/server/services/tinybird/TinybirdService.js`, this PR made two JWT changes outside its stated scope. Revert both. (1) Line 147: restore `{noTimestamp: true}` as the third argument to `jwt.sign`. (2) Line 164 in `_isJWTExpired`: restore `jwt.verify(token, this.tinybirdConfig.adminToken)` instead of `jwt.decode(token)`, so tokens with a bad signature or signed with a rotated secret are treated as expired. Keep the existing try/catch that returns true on error. Run `ghost/core/test/unit/server/services/tinybird/TinybirdService.test.js` afterwards.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE.md still lists the removed top_browsers/devices/os endpoints
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/server/data/tinybird/ARCHITECTURE.md` (around lines 253-256), remove the entries for `api_top_browsers`, `api_top_devices` and `api_top_os`. These endpoint pipes no longer exist and are no longer in `TINYBIRD_PIPES` in `ghost/core/core/server/services/tinybird/TinybirdService.js`. Also check whether the doc still lists device/browser/os as supported filter parameters on any endpoint, and update those mentions.

findings.title: Filter removal and test updates are consistent
findings.body:
The pipe changes are consistent. `device`, `browser` and `os` are removed from all four places they were defined (`api_kpis`, `api_top_locations`, `api_top_pages`, `filtered_sessions`). The stale commented-out `source` clause in `api_top_pages.pipe` is removed too, which makes sense because `filtered_sessions` handles source filtering.

The "multiple filters combined" YAML tests were repointed to `source=bing.com&pathname=/about/` instead of being deleted, so every `api_top_*` endpoint still has a test combining two filters.
